title: Relax: Composable Abstractions for End-to-End Dynamic Machine Learning
problem: Dynamic shape computations in modern ML workloads (especially LLMs) cannot be efficiently compiled by existing frameworks that treat computational graphs, loop-level tensor programs, and external library calls as separate, non-interoperable abstractions, preventing cross-level optimization and limiting deployment to diverse backends.
motivation: LLM adoption demands universal deployment across heterogeneous backends (GPUs, mobile, embedded, browsers), but dynamic shapes cause existing compilers to either fail or fall back to slow interpreted execution.
method: Relax builds a single unified representation (called a compiler IR, or intermediate representation) that describes three normally separate aspects of ML programs: high-level computational graphs, low-level loop-based tensor operations (called TIR), and calls to external libraries—all in one language. Instead of treating shape sizes (how big tensors are) as information that gets lost between these levels, Relax marks them as first-class values that flow through the entire program, enabling the compiler to optimize based on shape information at every stage. The compiler then uses this unified view to fuse multiple operations into single kernels (combining operations for speed), specialize operators for their actual inputs, and finally generate deployment code for GPUs, mobile phones (Android/iOS), embedded microcontrollers, and web-based targets (WebAssembly and WebGPU).
key_novelty: Relax unifies three separate aspects of ML programs (computational graphs, low-level tensor loop operations, and external library calls) with first-class symbolic shapes that flow throughout the program, enabling shape-aware optimizations that work across all these different levels.
contributions: Cross-level IR abstraction unifying computational graphs, loop-level tensor programs, and library calls
First-class symbolic shape annotations enabling dynamic-shape-aware cross-level optimization
End-to-end compilation framework competitive with SOTA on GPUs while enabling deployment to mobile, embedded, and browser backends
Open-source integration into Apache TVM ecosystem

metrics.speedup: performance competitive with SOTA systems on various GPUs
metrics.other: enables deployment to mobile phones, embedded devices, web browsers not supported by prior compilers

baselines: state-of-the-art ML compilation systems (unspecified in abstract)
limitations: Evaluation details on accuracy overhead of symbolic shape inference not discussed in abstract; compilation time for large dynamic models not analyzed.
primary_theme: unified dynamic-shape compiler abstraction for end-to-end ML
